Subject: Ordinex performance qualification - summary & action plan

Tim / Priya — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Call summary (high level):
- Goal: Confirm p95 / p99 end-to-end latency targets for your inference traffic and validate fit between Redwood Hosted API and your incumbent provider.
- Primary constraints: mixed streaming + non-streaming traffic (70/30), typical prompt length 120–250 tokens, 95th percentile SLA target ~120ms, 99th percentile target ~300ms (at your 2k RPS daytime peak).
- Key risks you called out: variability under concurrent streaming sessions, cold KV cache on long-tail user journeys, and geographic fanout to EU customers.

Immediate asks we agreed on:
1) You to share a small, anonymized traffic sample (CSV with timestamp, request_type, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, region) — we can work with a 10k-row day sample.
2) Redwood to run a focused qualification plan: synthetic replay of your profile against Hosted API and a matched environment on our dedicated runner to measure p95/p99 E2E (app-level proxy -> Redwood -> model -> response).
3) Agree on success criteria: p95 <= 150ms AND p99 <= 350ms for the mixed profile during a 15-minute steady-state run at scaled concurrency that matches your tail (we can refine).

Proposed immediate timeline: 
- Monday (Jun 21): you send sample traffic + any firewall/egress IP allowlist notes.
- Wed (Jun 23): Redwood runs a baseline synthetic replay against Hosted API and returns core metrics + sample traces.
- Thu (Jun 24): short sync to review results and next steps (can be async if preferred).

Attachments: call-recording-20270620.mp4 (internal stub) and ordx-p95p99-sample-traffic.csv (placeholder filename you can use when sharing).

Notes for internal team (cc’d): Soojin, we’ll need a quick runbook for streaming concurrency shapes (we saw you suggested 30–60s average stream length). Recommend we set up an isolated test harness that preserves client-side keepalive patterns.

Tim/Priya — do these next steps look right? Happy to tighten success thresholds if you prefer a more conservative ramp.

Best,
Mateo
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Tim — received the CSV, thanks. Quick update from our side after initial ingest and a short-run:

What we did in the baseline run:
- Converted your CSV into a replay profile that preserves request mix, token lengths, and streaming vs non-streaming ratios.
- Replayed against Redwood Hosted API in us-west-2 with a 15-minute steady-state at target concurrency (~2k RPS synthetic headroom) using the recommended batching configuration from Soojin.
- Collected E2E timings (client proxy -> Redwood -> model -> response) and sampled KV cold-start traces.

Preliminary results (hosted run):
- p50: 62ms
- p95: 132ms
- p99: 318ms
- Observations: streaming sessions show a longer tail when concurrency of open streams exceeds ~400 simultaneous streams. We saw periodic spikes tied to KV misses during sessions that start with longer prompts.

Next steps we propose (short):
1) Repeat the same replay against a matched environment where we disable prefix caching and enable a quantization profile closer to your production model so we can isolate the impact of caching + quantization.
2) Run a dedicated streaming-focused run where we keep the number of concurrent open streams as a knob (200/400/800) to observe p99 behavior and identify the concurrency inflection point.
3) Share representative trace samples and a short write-up of mitigations (batch tuning, prefix cache warmup, fallback model variant) — Marissa, can you draft the customer-facing summary?

Logistics: For the next runs we’ll need a 1-hour window when you can allow our test IPs (we’ll send a narrow list and timing). Also, do you prefer we run EU-region tests separately? If so, suggest we mirror the same profile in eu-west-1.

Attached: short replay-log-excerpt.csv (internal), call recording reference.

Mateo
AE | Redwood Inference
(On behalf of Soojin & Avery)

Ordinex performance qualification summary (draft)
Overview: We replayed a representative day of anonymized traffic against Redwood Hosted API in us-west-2. The replay preserves streaming vs non-streaming ratios and token length distributions.
Key measured outcomes (hosted): p95 = 132ms, p99 = 318ms (15-minute steady-state run at ~2k RPS synthetic).
Interpretation: Hosted API meets your stated p95 target (<=150ms) and is within a conservative p99 guardrail (<=350ms) on the mixed profile. Streaming concurrency is the primary driver of the tail — we recommend targeted tuning (keepalive shapes, prefix cache warmup, and batching limits) and a short targeted run to verify mitigations.
Action items (agreed):
- Redwood: run streaming-concurrency sweep (200/400/800) and a no-cache control run by Thu, Jun 24.
- Ordinex: provide a short 1-hour allowlist window for test IPs and confirm if EU mirroring is required.

If that reads OK, I’ll send this to Tim/Priya with the replay logs and a simple chart.
